To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the EMSs of Defectiveness/Shame, Insufficient Self Control, Vulnerability, and Incompetence/ Inferiority were associated, both concurrently and longitudinally, with perceptions of parenting; (2) the EMSs were also associated, both concurrently, with symptoms of depression; (3) the EMSs partially mediated the relationship between perceptions of parenting and symptoms of depression; and (4) the EMSs did not fully mediate the relationship.
the EMSs of vulnerability, defectiveness, and incompetence were related to parental perceptions of rejection and overprotectiveness and to depressive symptoms.
parental perceptions are related to EMSs which are related to depressive symptomatology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of parenting and early maladaptive schemas in the development of depression.
the development of a measure of the cognitive schemas of young adults, and the relationship of these cognitive schemas to depression.
the relationship between early maladaptive schemas, parenting perceptions, and depression in a sample consisting of 194 young adults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

parental perceptions of parenting, as well as the EMSs of defectivness/shame, insufficent self control, vulnerability and incompetence/inferority, are related to depressive symptomatology in young adults.
the results of this study support the cognitive model of depression and the role of parenting as an antecedent to depression.
the findings of the current study are consistent with the cognitive theory of depression, but do not provide strong support for the theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parenting, EMSs and depression are interrelated.
parenting, EMSs, and depression are all related to one another and that the relationship between parenting and depressive symptoms is partially mediated by EMSs.

the four schemas of defectiveness/sham, insufficient self control/vulnerability, and incompetence/ininferiority partially mediate the relationships between perceptions of parenting and symptoms of depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EMSs are important to consider when working with clients presenting with depressive symptomatology.
parenting has an important role to play in the development of cognitive schemas that can lead to depressive symptoms in young adults.
the EMSs that are most strongly associated with depression are also the most strongly associated with perceptions of parental behavior.
